rationale: Evidence from iteration 6 (kp 2.0, base_speed 1.1, kd 0.3, narrow five-sensor array) scored 354.2, the best raced design so far. The oval finished 16 of 20 runs (80%, up from 55% at kp 2.5). Oval line_loss_events fell to 0.85 (from 0.95), oval max_error fell to 0.048 (from 0.054), and s-bend line loss fell to 1.1 (from 1.25). Slalom line loss fell to 1.0 (from 1.15). The s-bend and slalom still end off track in all 40 trials, so they remain the main gap. Oval steering_oscillation is still 0.327, which is the highest jitter reading and the reason to test kd next. The Evaluator's rule applies: line loss fell and completion held above 50%, so kp 2.0 is kept and kd 0.25 is tested alone. Change: kd 0.3 to 0.25, with everything else unchanged (narrow geometry, base_speed 1.1, kp 2.0, ki 0, sensor_weights [2,1,0,-1,-2], last_direction). Expected result: oval steering_oscillation falls below about 0.3, oval completion holds at 70% or higher, and line_loss_events and max_error stay at or below iteration 6 levels. Risk: lower kd gives less damping on the tighter bends, so line loss could rise. If it does, the next step is to revert kd to 0.3 and test base_speed 1.2 alone. Hypotheses to test: (a) kd 0.25 cuts oscillation without losing the line; (b) the s-bend and slalom failures come from line loss at the bends, not from sensor coverage. Measurements requested: per-track completion, progress, completion_time, line_loss_events, max_error and steering_oscillation, so the kd effect can be isolated from the kp 2.0 baseline.
